repositories.brief_summary: POWER gained frame pointer support and new Uchar/runtime helpers landed, alongside backend codegen work for sqrt/atomics on power, riscv and s390x.
repositories.new_features_summary: Frame pointers on POWER, new Uchar ASCII/Latin-1 helpers, caml_result_find_exception, and a non-allocating Runtime_events.User.write.
repositories.new_features:
- POWER now maintains an ELFv2 **frame pointer** in r31 (allocation pointer moved to r23), enabling stack unwinding tools on ppc64le; merged after [Tim McGilchrist](https://github.com/tmcgilchrist) tracked down a TOC-register corruption in `caml_runstack` during effect handling, with review from [Zane Hambly](https://github.com/Zaneham) and [Olivier Nicole](https://github.com/OlivierNicole) ([#14505](https://github.com/ocaml/ocaml/issues/14505)).
- New `Stdlib.Uchar.{is_ascii, ascii_to_char, is_latin1, latin1_to_char}` functions were added, with `is_char`/`of_char`/`to_char` now documented as deprecated aliases in favour of the more explicit names ([#14981](https://github.com/ocaml/ocaml/issues/14981)).
- A `caml_result_find_exception` inline helper was added to `runtime/caml/mlvalues.h`, giving C code a pointer-based accessor to extract an exception from a `caml_result` without constructing an invalid `value`, implemented by [Gabriel Scherer](https://github.com/gasche) ([#14814](https://github.com/ocaml/ocaml/issues/14814)).
- `Runtime_events.User.write` no longer allocates in the common single-threaded case: the per-thread list-based write-buffer cache was replaced with a single atomic bytes slot in domain-local storage, cutting roughly 23 words/event of allocation, by [Anil Madhavapeddy](https://github.com/avsm) ([#14984](https://github.com/ocaml/ocaml/issues/14984)).
- The let-rec safety check now gives **generic arrays dynamic size**, fixing an unsoundness where floats and addresses differ in size on 32-bit systems, by [Jeremy Yallop](https://github.com/yallop) ([#14993](https://github.com/ocaml/ocaml/issues/14993)).
- The type checker no longer assumes abstract types defined in the current module are injective or contractive, closing a soundness gap, by [Jeremy Yallop](https://github.com/yallop) ([#14982](https://github.com/ocaml/ocaml/issues/14982)).
- Fixed a **build reproducibility** bug where the generic `%.cmi`/`%.cmx` rules in the root Makefile raced with `otherlibs/{str,unix}`'s own build rules under `make -j`, changing recorded interface digests non-deterministically, by [Bernhard M. Wiedemann](https://github.com/bmwiedemann) ([#14989](https://github.com/ocaml/ocaml/issues/14989)).
- Fixed a missing newline after `Pexp_unreachable` in `printast`, by [David Allsopp](https://github.com/dra27) ([#14992](https://github.com/ocaml/ocaml/issues/14992)).
- Corrected a cross-reference in the `Changes` file pointing `#14891` at the wrong issue number, by [Antonin Décimo](https://github.com/MisterDA) ([#14994](https://github.com/ocaml/ocaml/issues/14994)).
repositories.activity_summary: Six new PRs were opened for backend codegen and runtime-events work, while several long-open PRs were declined by the stdlib team.
repositories.activity:
- [Tim McGilchrist](https://github.com/tmcgilchrist) opened a fix making the runtime-events ring buffer's total size a `size_t` to avoid a 32-bit integer overflow that corrupts the ring past 2 GiB ([#15000](https://github.com/ocaml/ocaml/issues/15000)), addressing the issue he reported the same day ([#14999](https://github.com/ocaml/ocaml/issues/14999)); he also opened a PR adding an `EV_C_MAJOR_DIRECT_ALLOCATED_WORDS` runtime-events counter to distinguish direct major-heap allocations from promotions ([#15001](https://github.com/ocaml/ocaml/issues/15001)).
- [Zane Hambly](https://github.com/Zaneham) opened a series of per-architecture native-codegen PRs emitting `fsqrt`/`fsqrt.d` instead of C calls for square root on s390x, riscv and power, plus byte-swap intrinsics on s390x ([#15002](https://github.com/ocaml/ocaml/issues/15002), [#15005](https://github.com/ocaml/ocaml/issues/15005), [#15006](https://github.com/ocaml/ocaml/issues/15006)).
- [Antonin Décimo](https://github.com/MisterDA) opened a CI change enabling KVM hardware acceleration for Android emulator jobs, saving roughly 40s per CI run ([#15003](https://github.com/ocaml/ocaml/issues/15003)), and continues to push the 32-bit Y2K38/large-file-support PR ([#14997](https://github.com/ocaml/ocaml/issues/14997)) and the Autoconf-based C++ compiler detection fix ([#14996](https://github.com/ocaml/ocaml/issues/14996)) toward merge.
- [Romain Beauxis](https://github.com/toots) opened and then closed `caml_result_format_exception` after being pointed to the equivalent, already-in-review `caml_result_find_exception` by [Nicolás Ojeda Bär](https://github.com/nojb) ([#14998](https://github.com/ocaml/ocaml/issues/14998), [#14814](https://github.com/ocaml/ocaml/issues/14814)).
- [Stefan Muenzel](https://github.com/smuenzel) continues iterating on a draft PR shrinking AMD64 stack-reallocation code by avoiding stack-passed parameters, working through register-safety objections from [Xavier Leroy](https://github.com/xavierleroy) about PLT-stub clobbering of r10/r11 ([#14954](https://github.com/ocaml/ocaml/issues/14954)).
- [Zane Hambly](https://github.com/Zaneham) also has an open PR generating native atomic exchange and compare-and-set across amd64, arm64, riscv, power and s390x by gating on immediate types ([#14980](https://github.com/ocaml/ocaml/issues/14980)); [Anarchos](https://github.com/Sylvain78) continues Haiku platform fixes for Unix socket tests, `setlocale` thread-safety and signal handling ([#14773](https://github.com/ocaml/ocaml/issues/14773)); [Gabriel Scherer](https://github.com/gasche) is iterating on a `Weak.Make` reimplementation using open-addressing with linear probing that shows up to 2.8x speedups in hash-consing benchmarks ([#14979](https://github.com/ocaml/ocaml/issues/14979)); [Jeremy Yallop](https://github.com/yallop) opened a fix so `Weak.get_copy` no longer unsafely shallow-copies continuations, which could segfault ([#14988](https://github.com/ocaml/ocaml/issues/14988)).
- [Török Edwin](https://github.com/edwintorok) merged a testsuite addition that fragments GC sizeclass pools to guard against a regression previously fixed by GC work-accounting changes ([#14818](https://github.com/ocaml/ocaml/issues/14818)).
- The standard library team, represented by [Daniel Bünzli](https://github.com/dbuenzli), closed [Benoit](https://github.com/benjub)'s `Stdlib.Char.Ascii.is_punct` addition as out of scope ([#14957](https://github.com/ocaml/ocaml/issues/14957)) and closed [Christophe Raffalli](https://github.com/craff)'s `Unix.nonblock_single_write`/`Unix.nonblock_read` PR pending a broader review of C bindings, while proposing a `domain_blocking`/`domain_non_blocking` naming convention for future non-blocking I/O primitives ([#13024](https://github.com/ocaml/ocaml/issues/13024)).
- [Zane Hambly](https://github.com/Zaneham) closed his own `endbr64`-landing-pad PR for amd64 CET support, citing unresolved MSVC failures ([#14515](https://github.com/ocaml/ocaml/issues/14515)), which superseded [Dave Voutila](https://github.com/voutilad)'s earlier OpenBSD `endbr64` PR ([#13023](https://github.com/ocaml/ocaml/issues/13023)).
repositories.discussions_summary: Discussion centered on runtime-events reliability, a Weak.get_copy safety bug, and naming conventions for future non-blocking C bindings.
repositories.notable_discussions:
- [Mattias](https://github.com/mattiasdrp) reported that custom runtime events behave inconsistently under fast-paced event emission, sometimes raising `Runtime_events: corrupt stream`; [Sadiq Jaffer](https://github.com/sadiqj) clarified that dropping events under load is by design but agreed the corrupt-stream failure is a real bug to fix ([#14151](https://github.com/ocaml/ocaml/issues/14151)), which connects to the ring-buffer overflow root-caused this week ([#14999](https://github.com/ocaml/ocaml/issues/14999), [#15000](https://github.com/ocaml/ocaml/issues/15000)).
- [Stephen Dolan](https://github.com/stedolan) and [Josh Berdine](https://github.com/jberdine) discussed whether `Weak.get_copy` should be deprecated in favour of `Weak.get` given its long history of correctness pitfalls, in the thread around [Jeremy Yallop](https://github.com/yallop)'s continuation-copy safety fix ([#14988](https://github.com/ocaml/ocaml/issues/14988)).
- [Gabriel Scherer](https://github.com/gasche) reflected on PR-merging norms in the project, noting that maintainers other than himself and Octachron are welcome to merge reviewed PRs, in the discussion on [#14814](https://github.com/ocaml/ocaml/issues/14814).
- [Daniel Bünzli](https://github.com/dbuenzli), on behalf of the standard library team, proposed an informal RFC for naming C bindings using `domain_blocking`/`domain_non_blocking` qualifiers instead of describing the runtime lock directly, prompted by [#13024](https://github.com/ocaml/ocaml/issues/13024).
repositories.trends_summary: Continued push for backend codegen parity on POWER, RISC-V and s390x, alongside a cluster of runtime-events correctness and performance fixes.
repositories.emerging_trends:
- Backend codegen parity work continues to expand to less-common architectures, with [Zane Hambly](https://github.com/Zaneham) driving native `sqrt`/byte-swap emission on s390x, riscv and power ([#15002](https://github.com/ocaml/ocaml/issues/15002), [#15005](https://github.com/ocaml/ocaml/issues/15005), [#15006](https://github.com/ocaml/ocaml/issues/15006)) and native atomic exchange/CAS across five architectures ([#14980](https://github.com/ocaml/ocaml/issues/14980)), following on from the POWER frame-pointer work ([#14505](https://github.com/ocaml/ocaml/issues/14505)).
- The runtime-events subsystem is receiving concentrated attention: a ring-buffer overflow on large configurations ([#14999](https://github.com/ocaml/ocaml/issues/14999), [#15000](https://github.com/ocaml/ocaml/issues/15000)), a non-allocating write path ([#14984](https://github.com/ocaml/ocaml/issues/14984)), a new GC counter ([#15001](https://github.com/ocaml/ocaml/issues/15001)), and an open reliability report ([#14151](https://github.com/ocaml/ocaml/issues/14151)) all landed or were discussed in the same week, suggesting growing production use of the profiling API.
- 32-bit correctness and build reproducibility keep surfacing as themes, spanning Y2K38/large-file support ([#14997](https://github.com/ocaml/ocaml/issues/14997)), the ring-buffer integer overflow fix ([#15000](https://github.com/ocaml/ocaml/issues/15000)), and the otherlibs Makefile race ([#14989](https://github.com/ocaml/ocaml/issues/14989)).

repositories.brief_summary: opam init --reinit's 2.1-upgrade retry loop was fixed and reftest flakiness addressed, while review of #7068 surfaced new switch-state edge cases.
repositories.new_features_summary: Fixed opam init --reinit looping after a 2.1-root upgrade and added debug logging for incremental repository diff loading.
repositories.new_features:
- Fixed `opam init --reinit` exiting with status 10 and prompting users to re-run the command after upgrading an opam 2.1 root, so upgrades now complete in a single invocation ([#7058](https://github.com/ocaml/opam/pull/7058), fixes [#7057](https://github.com/ocaml/opam/issues/7057)) by [Kate](https://github.com/kit-ty-kate)
- Added level 4 **debug output** listing the patch operations applied when a repository is loaded incrementally from a diff, aiding diagnosis of incremental-loading bugs such as [#6872](https://github.com/ocaml/opam/issues/6872) ([#7072](https://github.com/ocaml/opam/pull/7072)) by [Kate](https://github.com/kit-ty-kate)
- Test-suite `git` invocations now disable `gc.autoDetach` and `maintenance.autoDetach`, removing a source of the random `patchDiff` failures on macOS ([#7069](https://github.com/ocaml/opam/pull/7069), fixes [#7037](https://github.com/ocaml/opam/issues/7037)) by [Kate](https://github.com/kit-ty-kate)
- Test suite no longer generates files with **CRLF line endings**, resolving spurious failures surfaced while working on [#7058](https://github.com/ocaml/opam/pull/7058) ([#7071](https://github.com/ocaml/opam/pull/7071)) by [Kate](https://github.com/kit-ty-kate)
repositories.activity_summary: Four PRs merged fixing init and test flakiness, while newly opened PRs target docs, git-gc handling, and the PowerShell init script.
repositories.activity:
- Newly opened work includes a documentation fix for **conjunctions in conflict version formulas** by [Ryan Gibb](https://github.com/RyanGibb) ([#7082](https://github.com/ocaml/opam/pull/7082)), a draft always printing **empty lists** when printing bindings by [Kate](https://github.com/kit-ty-kate) that depends on ocaml/opam-file-format#66 ([#7080](https://github.com/ocaml/opam/pull/7080)), a draft to disable **git gc/maintenance** on repositories opam manages ([#7073](https://github.com/ocaml/opam/pull/7073)), and a fix for the generated **PowerShell init script** missing required parentheses around its `if` condition by [Flandia](https://github.com/flandia), now covered by a Windows reftest ([#7070](https://github.com/ocaml/opam/pull/7070))
- [Kate](https://github.com/kit-ty-kate) merged four PRs this week: the `opam init --reinit` retry-loop fix ([#7058](https://github.com/ocaml/opam/pull/7058)), the debug-logging addition ([#7072](https://github.com/ocaml/opam/pull/7072)), the `patchDiff` git-maintenance fix ([#7069](https://github.com/ocaml/opam/pull/7069)), and the CRLF testsuite fix ([#7071](https://github.com/ocaml/opam/pull/7071))
- [Kate](https://github.com/kit-ty-kate)'s PR reworking `opam init --reinit` to **regenerate the list of valid switches** and their cache remains under review by [R. Boujbel](https://github.com/rjbou), who requested more targeted tests and flagged that the change should also cover the `switch-config` file; the review surfaced two follow-up bugs — an inconsistent cache when an installed package definition is missing ([#7078](https://github.com/ocaml/opam/issues/7078)) and untested global-switch fixups ([#7077](https://github.com/ocaml/opam/issues/7077)) — tracked against the main PR ([#7068](https://github.com/ocaml/opam/pull/7068))

- [Kate](https://github.com/kit-ty-kate)'s PR to respect `safe_mode` when an on-disk cache is outdated, which also fixed `opam list --debug --safe` silently dropping debug logs ([#7000](https://github.com/ocaml/opam/issues/7000)), is open awaiting review ([#7067](https://github.com/ocaml/opam/pull/7067))
- [Onyeka Obi](https://github.com/MavenRain)'s PR correcting **package-name inference** for dotted/hidden project directories was closed without merging despite fixing the reported bug ([#7063](https://github.com/ocaml/opam/pull/7063), targets [#7043](https://github.com/ocaml/opam/issues/7043))
repositories.discussions_summary: Discussions covered AI-assisted contribution policy, the design of an opam lock dependency-exclusion flag, and switch invariant printing.
repositories.notable_discussions:
- [Onyeka Obi](https://github.com/MavenRain) asked for clarification after their package-name-inference fix was closed without comment, questioning whether AI-assisted contributions are accepted and offering to rework the patch if the concern is scope rather than authorship ([#7063](https://github.com/ocaml/opam/pull/7063))
- [Pierre Villemot](https://github.com/Halbaroth) proposed an `--ignore` flag for `opam lock` to exclude optional dependencies from generated lockfiles; [Kate](https://github.com/kit-ty-kate) pushed back that an implicit ignore is dangerous if a dependency later becomes mandatory, suggesting an explicit `--ignore-optional-dependency` name instead ([#7076](https://github.com/ocaml/opam/issues/7076))
- [R. Boujbel](https://github.com/rjbou) and [Kate](https://github.com/kit-ty-kate) traced why switch **invariants get recomputed** repeatedly on empty switches to the `OpamFormat` printer never emitting empty-list fields, a fix attempted in a draft PR ([#7080](https://github.com/ocaml/opam/pull/7080)) that currently fails its tests ([#7079](https://github.com/ocaml/opam/issues/7079))
- [Pierre Villemot](https://github.com/Halbaroth) reported that `opam sw --switch foo show` succeeds silently for a nonexistent switch instead of failing, which [Kate](https://github.com/kit-ty-kate) agreed should be fixed ([#7075](https://github.com/ocaml/opam/issues/7075))

repositories.brief_summary: Two client-facing code-action bugs were fixed (create-counterpart capability checks, unused-code quick fixes) while an odoc navigable-references PR was opened.
repositories.new_features_summary: Fixed unused-code quick fixes and capability-gated file-creation in code actions, both merged and documented in CHANGES.md.
repositories.new_features:
- Unused-code quick fixes (`Remove unused open/type/module/constructor/case/rec`, `Mark as unused`) are offered again: the diagnostic matcher previously expected message text Merlin never emits, such as `Warning 33: unused open B.`, so almost none of these actions ever appeared; the fix also stops `open!` from being rewritten to `open!!` by classifying diagnostics by warning number instead of matching on bare substrings, and restricts the old textual fallback to Dune-sourced diagnostics so alert payloads containing text like `unused open` cannot trigger destructive edits by [emre](https://github.com/dayangac) ([#2117](https://github.com/ocaml/ocaml-lsp/issues/2117), fixes [#2116](https://github.com/ocaml/ocaml-lsp/issues/2116))
- The "open related source" code action no longer attaches a `CreateFile` workspace edit for clients that cannot apply it: it now checks `workspace.workspaceEdit.documentChanges` together with the client's advertised resource operations via a new `Capabilities.workspace_edit_resource_operation` check, and only offers file creation when both are supported, avoiding a follow-up `window/showDocument` call against a file that was never created by [emre](https://github.com/dayangac) ([#2115](https://github.com/ocaml/ocaml-lsp/issues/2115), fixes [#2114](https://github.com/ocaml/ocaml-lsp/issues/2114))

- [Rudi Grinberg](https://github.com/rgrinberg) added a fake Dune RPC server for black-box e2e tests that speaks the initialize/version-negotiation/diagnostic/progress protocol without a real `dune build -w` process ([#2123](https://github.com/ocaml/ocaml-lsp/issues/2123)), then used it to add coverage for Dune/Merlin diagnostic merging and removal ([#2134](https://github.com/ocaml/ocaml-lsp/issues/2134)), location-free diagnostics and unknown-promotion removal ([#2135](https://github.com/ocaml/ocaml-lsp/issues/2135)), the `ocamllsp/show-merlin-config` command ([#2127](https://github.com/ocaml/ocaml-lsp/issues/2127)), and the definition request on non-Merlin documents ([#2124](https://github.com/ocaml/ocaml-lsp/issues/2124), [#2140](https://github.com/ocaml/ocaml-lsp/issues/2140))

- [emre](https://github.com/dayangac) added tests covering the create-counterpart client capabilities (a client advertising the create resource operation, and one advertising neither) ahead of the capability-gating fix ([#2119](https://github.com/ocaml/ocaml-lsp/issues/2119))

repositories.brief_summary: Discussion continued on [#2072](https://github.com/ocaml/merlin/issues/2072), the LRgrep syntax-error-message integration, including whether it belongs upstream in the OCaml compiler.
repositories.activity_summary: The LRgrep-based syntax error message integration PR remained open, with discussion on its scope and eventual upstreaming.
repositories.activity:
- The **LRgrep integration** PR by [Frédéric Bour](https://github.com/let-def) remains open and under discussion ([#2072](https://github.com/ocaml/merlin/issues/2072)); it adds a declarative error-message specification (`src/ocaml/preprocess/parse_errors.lrgrep`), a `make lrgrep-coverage` target that produces a `coverage.md` report of grammar constructs still lacking error messages, and a vendored LRgrep runtime following the existing MenhirLib vendoring pattern, all as an additive change that does not alter existing parser behavior.
- The PR currently shows a **conflicting merge status**, indicating it needs a rebase before it can move forward ([#2072](https://github.com/ocaml/merlin/issues/2072)).
repositories.discussions_summary: Contributors debated whether the LRgrep-based error-message work should target the OCaml compiler rather than Merlin.
repositories.notable_discussions:
- On [#2072](https://github.com/ocaml/merlin/issues/2072), [Olivier Nicole](https://github.com/OlivierNicole) asked whether the LRgrep error-message work should also (or instead) go into the compiler itself, tagging [Florian Angeletti](https://github.com/Octachron) and [Gabriel Scherer](https://github.com/gasche) for input.
- [Gabriel Scherer](https://github.com/gasche) responded that upstream is interested, noting this completes a **better-syntax-error-messages** effort that [Frédéric Bour](https://github.com/let-def) started with [ocaml/ocaml#33](https://github.com/ocaml/ocaml/issues/33) in 2014, and suggested Merlin is serving as a testbed partly because its existing error-handling machinery and its position relative to the oxcaml/ocaml gap make integration easier there first ([#2072](https://github.com/ocaml/merlin/issues/2072)).
repositories.trends_summary: Interest in improving OCaml syntax error messages spans both Merlin and the upstream compiler, with Merlin used as an integration testbed.
repositories.emerging_trends: - Renewed focus on **syntax error message quality**, with Merlin positioned as a testbed for changes ([#2072](https://github.com/ocaml/merlin/issues/2072)) that maintainers ultimately hope to see adopted in the upstream OCaml compiler, continuing an effort traced back to [ocaml/ocaml#33](https://github.com/ocaml/ocaml/issues/33).

repositories.brief_summary: Dune language version bumped to 3.25 with a Melange artifact variable and a large internal engine performance rewrite by rgrinberg.
repositories.new_features_summary: New `%{melange.emit:...}` variable, `(flags ...)` for ocamllex/ocamlyacc, opt-in SAT tracing, and sha256 checksums ship under dune-lang 3.25.
repositories.new_features:
- Added the `%{melange.emit:<target-dir>}` artifact variable so a `dune` file can reference and depend on the output directory of a `melange.emit` stanza, resolved relative to the referencing file ([#15751](https://github.com/ocaml/dune/issues/15751), [#15827](https://github.com/ocaml/dune/issues/15827), by [Antonio Nuno Monteiro](https://github.com/anmonteiro)); this required a following fix for Melange emission with installed libraries whose `.cmj`/`.cmi` files live under a `melange` object directory, resolving [#14820](https://github.com/ocaml/dune/issues/14820) ([#15949](https://github.com/ocaml/dune/issues/15949), [#15900](https://github.com/ocaml/dune/issues/15900), [#15950](https://github.com/ocaml/dune/issues/15950), [#15967](https://github.com/ocaml/dune/issues/15967))
- Added `(flags ...)` support to the `ocamllex` and `ocamlyacc` stanzas so custom options can be passed to the parser generators, by [Rudi Grinberg](https://github.com/rgrinberg) ([#15907](https://github.com/ocaml/dune/issues/15907))
- Added an opt-in `sat` trace category emitting a `sat/solve` event with the SAT solver's variables, clauses, decisions, conflicts, and duration, enabled via `DUNE_TRACE=+sat`; described as preliminary observability for the single-solve package-solver effort, by [Ali Caglayan](https://github.com/Alizter) ([#15923](https://github.com/ocaml/dune/issues/15923), [#15961](https://github.com/ocaml/dune/issues/15961))
- Source archives lacking a published checksum now use **sha256** instead of md5, by [Shun Ueda](https://github.com/shunueda) ([#15824](https://github.com/ocaml/dune/issues/15824))
- **BREAKING CHANGE**: `(warnings (duplicate_deps ..))` in `dune-project` now requires dune language version 3.22 instead of 3.18, by [@v-gb](https://github.com/v-gb) ([#15696](https://github.com/ocaml/dune/issues/15696))
- Fixed `enabled_if` on `install` stanzas not being respected when adding files/directories to the `@all` alias, resolving [#15825](https://github.com/ocaml/dune/issues/15825), by [@aryemans](https://github.com/aryemans) ([#15895](https://github.com/ocaml/dune/issues/15895), [#15912](https://github.com/ocaml/dune/issues/15912))
- Fixed Git-patch application truncating unquoted filenames with spaces at the first space, preserving the full path, by [Rudi Grinberg](https://github.com/rgrinberg) ([#15781](https://github.com/ocaml/dune/issues/15781))
- Dune's own language version bumped to 3.25 with regenerated opam files, meaning several of this week's features (Melange artifact variable, ocamllex/ocamlyacc flags) require projects to adopt lang 3.25 to use them, by [Rudi Grinberg](https://github.com/rgrinberg) ([#15919](https://github.com/ocaml/dune/issues/15919))
- Landlock-based sandbox confinement for directly-executed sandboxed actions proposed, restricting writes to the action sandbox, temp directory, trace directory, and `/dev`, with `DUNE_CONFIG__LANDLOCK=disabled` as an escape hatch — opened but not yet merged, by [Rudi Grinberg](https://github.com/rgrinberg) ([#15858](https://github.com/ocaml/dune/issues/15858))
- Documented the `%{melange.emit:...}` artifact variable in the Melange manual with worked examples of relative path expansion, by [Antonio Nuno Monteiro](https://github.com/anmonteiro) ([#15827](https://github.com/ocaml/dune/issues/15827))
- Documented the new `(flags ...)` fields for `ocamllex` and `ocamlyacc` in the stanza reference ([#15907](https://github.com/ocaml/dune/issues/15907))

repositories.brief_summary: No commits landed on master this week; activity centered on open-PR discussion for OxCaml include-functor support and odoc_driver stdlib-detection fixes.
repositories.activity_summary: Two PRs opened (Stdlib polyfill pattern, `Forward removal) while ongoing PRs advanced on include functor support and driver stdlib detection.
repositories.activity:
- [Marek Kubica](https://github.com/Leonidas-from-XIV) opened [#1476](https://github.com/ocaml/odoc/pull/1476) proposing a **Stdlib polyfill pattern** so odoc can fall back to its own extensions only when the compiler's Stdlib lacks a function, prompted by a `List.partition_map` build failure on OCaml 4.11.
- [Marek Kubica](https://github.com/Leonidas-from-XIV) also opened [#1478](https://github.com/ocaml/odoc/pull/1478), a draft PR investigating removal of the apparently unused `` `Forward`` constructor after confirming it compiles and passes tests without it.
- The **include functor support for OxCaml** PR ([#1452](https://github.com/ocaml/odoc/pull/1452)) by [Marek Kubica](https://github.com/Leonidas-from-XIV) progressed substantially, implementing [Jon Ludlam](https://github.com/jonludlam)'s proposal to compile `include functor` down to a generated module plus functor application, resolving earlier cross-referencing concerns and removing the interim `allow_functor` machinery.
- The **odoc_driver stdlib-detection fix** for `$prefix/lib64` layouts ([#1474](https://github.com/ocaml/odoc/pull/1474)) by [@katrinafyi](https://github.com/katrinafyi) continued with a changelog update and a lower-bound bump on `ocamlfind` (>= 1.9.8) flagged by [Marek Kubica](https://github.com/Leonidas-from-XIV), and is tied to the newly filed [#1477](https://github.com/ocaml/odoc/issues/1477).
- The **multi-line link fix** for [#865](https://github.com/ocaml/odoc/issues/865) ([#1439](https://github.com/ocaml/odoc/pull/1439)) by [Tim ats](https://github.com/Tim-ats-d) remains open pending a polyfill for `String.fold_left`, missing before OCaml 4.13.
repositories.discussions_summary: Discussion focused on cross-referencing generated functor modules and the risk of silently overriding future Stdlib additions.
repositories.notable_discussions:
- On [#1452](https://github.com/ocaml/odoc/pull/1452), [Marek Kubica](https://github.com/Leonidas-from-XIV) and [Jon Ludlam](https://github.com/jonludlam) discussed how to cross-reference items produced by expanded `include functor` applications back to the original functor rather than to internally generated wrapper modules, eventually settling on a revised compilation scheme.
- On [#1476](https://github.com/ocaml/odoc/pull/1476), [Daniel Bünzli](https://github.com/dbuenzli) raised concerns that automatically preferring the compiler's Stdlib implementations over odoc's own could silently change semantics (e.g. iteration order) when new Stdlib versions are adopted, making bugs harder to trace.
- [@katrinafyi](https://github.com/katrinafyi) filed [#1477](https://github.com/ocaml/odoc/issues/1477) describing how opam installing the OCaml stdlib into `$prefix/lib64` (observed on openSUSE Tumbleweed with opam 2.5.2) breaks `odoc_driver`'s module detection, directly motivating [#1474](https://github.com/ocaml/odoc/pull/1474).
- On [#1475](https://github.com/ocaml/odoc/issues/1475), [@katrinafyi](https://github.com/katrinafyi) shared a work-in-progress fix (at `rsc-s/odoc` branch `subdirs`) for locating source files behind Dune's `include_subdirs qualified` wrapper modules, noting a risk of filename collisions since files are currently matched by basename only.
repositories.trends_summary: Work continues to harden odoc_driver against opam/findlib layout variations and Dune's module-wrapping edge cases.
repositories.emerging_trends:
- Repeated attention to **odoc_driver robustness** across differing opam/findlib installation layouts, spanning the `$prefix/lib64` stdlib detection issue ([#1477](https://github.com/ocaml/odoc/issues/1477), [#1474](https://github.com/ocaml/odoc/pull/1474)) and Dune's `include_subdirs qualified` wrapper-module source lookup ([#1475](https://github.com/ocaml/odoc/issues/1475)).
- Ongoing **OCaml version-compatibility considerations**, including a proposed Stdlib polyfill pattern ([#1476](https://github.com/ocaml/odoc/pull/1476)) and a missing-function issue on OCaml versions before 4.13 blocking [#1439](https://github.com/ocaml/odoc/pull/1439).
- Continued maturation of **OxCaml include-functor support** ([#1452](https://github.com/ocaml/odoc/pull/1452)), moving from an initial implementation toward a cleaner compilation scheme for cross-referencing.
repositories.contributors_summary: Marek Kubica advanced functor and stdlib-compatibility work while katrinafyi drove driver-detection fixes and filed new issues.
repositories.contributors:
- [Marek Kubica](https://github.com/Leonidas-from-XIV) progressed the **include functor** implementation for OxCaml ([#1452](https://github.com/ocaml/odoc/pull/1452)), opened a **Stdlib polyfill pattern** PR ([#1476](https://github.com/ocaml/odoc/pull/1476)), opened a draft PR investigating removal of the unused `` `Forward`` constructor ([#1478](https://github.com/ocaml/odoc/pull/1478)), and reviewed the `ocamlfind` version constraints needed for [#1474](https://github.com/ocaml/odoc/pull/1474).
- [@katrinafyi](https://github.com/katrinafyi) filed a new issue on stdlib detection in `$prefix/lib64` installs ([#1477](https://github.com/ocaml/odoc/issues/1477)), updated the changelog and iterated on the corresponding fix ([#1474](https://github.com/ocaml/odoc/pull/1474)), and shared a work-in-progress branch addressing Dune `include_subdirs qualified` source lookup on [#1475](https://github.com/ocaml/odoc/issues/1475).
- [Daniel Bünzli](https://github.com/dbuenzli) reviewed [#1476](https://github.com/ocaml/odoc/pull/1476), providing feedback on the risks of implicitly overriding local implementations with future Stdlib changes.
- [Jon Ludlam](https://github.com/jonludlam) participated in design discussion on [#1452](https://github.com/ocaml/odoc/pull/1452), proposing the compilation approach for `include functor` that was subsequently implemented, and was referenced in [#1474](https://github.com/ocaml/odoc/pull/1474)'s discussion around filing a follow-up issue.
- [Tim ats](https://github.com/Tim-ats-d) continues work on the multi-line link fix for [#865](https://github.com/ocaml/odoc/issues/865) via [#1439](https://github.com/ocaml/odoc/pull/1439), with review feedback on missing stdlib functions for older OCaml compatibility.

repositories.new_features_summary: New affect and dune-rpc-eio packages, a prometheus core/Lwt split, a jsont integer-range breaking change, and mirage-xen grant-copy support.
repositories.new_features:
- New **affect** 0.0.0 package published, a streamlined effects-based concurrency model for OCaml supported by an OCaml Software Foundation grant, by [Daniel Bünzli](https://github.com/dbuenzli) ([#30469](https://github.com/ocaml/opam-repository/pull/30469))
- New **dune-rpc-eio** 0.1.0 package: an Eio client for dune's RPC protocol that can spawn or attach to a dune server, build paths/aliases, run tests, and read diagnostics, by [Anil Madhavapeddy](https://github.com/avsm) ([#30453](https://github.com/ocaml/opam-repository/pull/30453))
- **mirage-xen** 9.0.1 adds `Import.copy_from`/`Import.copy_to`, hypervisor-mediated grant-copy primitives that speed up transfers such as the qubes-mirage-firewall, by [Hannes Mehnert](https://github.com/hannesm) ([#30493](https://github.com/ocaml/opam-repository/pull/30493))
- **prometheus** 1.4 splits the library into a synchronous core and a new **prometheus-lwt** package, deprecating the Lwt-typed timing helpers in core ahead of their eventual removal, by [Anil Madhavapeddy](https://github.com/avsm) with [Mark Elvers](https://github.com/mtelvers) ([#30452](https://github.com/ocaml/opam-repository/pull/30452))
- **jsont** 0.3.0 narrows the safely encodable integer range for `Jsont.int`/`Jsont.int64` from `[-2^53;2^53]` to `[-2^53+1;2^53-1]` (a breaking change; `Jsont.legacy_int`/`legacy_int64` are provided for migration), and fixes nested out-of-order case-member decoding, by [Daniel Bünzli](https://github.com/dbuenzli) ([#30485](https://github.com/ocaml/opam-repository/pull/30485))
- **sqlite3** 5.4.2 fixes OCaml GC rooting across runtime-released SQLite calls, preventing statement/database wrappers from being finalized while blocked inside SQLite, by [Markus Mottl](https://github.com/mmottl) ([#30475](https://github.com/ocaml/opam-repository/pull/30475))
- **ocamlmig** updated to OCaml 5.5 and its `[@@migrate]` attribute now accepts a `~min_version` for dependencies, letting `ocamlmig mig` add or update version constraints in `dune-project`, by [v-gb](https://github.com/v-gb) ([#30396](https://github.com/ocaml/opam-repository/pull/30396))
- **introcaml** alpha1 release adds flambda compiler support, by [Frédéric Bour](https://github.com/let-def) ([#30415](https://github.com/ocaml/opam-repository/pull/30415))
- New packages published this week: **checked_oint** 2.1.0, checked integer arithmetic, by [@hirrolot](https://github.com/hirrolot) ([#30505](https://github.com/ocaml/opam-repository/pull/30505)); **bitflyer** and **gmocoin** cryptocurrency-exchange API clients by [YOSHIHIRO Imai](https://github.com/yoshihiro503) ([#30459](https://github.com/ocaml/opam-repository/pull/30459), [#30460](https://github.com/ocaml/opam-repository/pull/30460)); **intel_hex** 0.4 and **bytream** 0.1 by [Михаил](https://github.com/dx3mod) ([#30487](https://github.com/ocaml/opam-repository/pull/30487), [#30458](https://github.com/ocaml/opam-repository/pull/30458)); the 4-package pure-OCaml Neo4j driver **neodriver** by [Tomasz Barański](https://github.com/tomob) ([#30448](https://github.com/ocaml/opam-repository/pull/30448)); and **p4spectec** 0.1.2, a P4-language mechanization toolchain, by [Haechan Kwon](https://github.com/pacokwon) ([#30455](https://github.com/ocaml/opam-repository/pull/30455))
- The **mirage-crypto-rng-\*** platform-specific packages (apart from the `mirage` and `mkernel` variants) are now marked deprecated, by [Hannes Mehnert](https://github.com/hannesm) ([#30478](https://github.com/ocaml/opam-repository/pull/30478))

repositories.brief_summary: Atomic block-index primitives landed, flambda2 int-id/rec-info internals were reworked, and Merlin was resynced with the frontend.
repositories.new_features_summary: New `Idx_atomic` module for atomic block indices, a `-gno-ocamldebug-types` flag, and a reworked redundant-modifier warning.
repositories.new_features:
- New `Idx_atomic` module in `stdlib_stable` exposes `get`/`set` externals for atomic block indices (`('a, 'b) idx_atomic`), following on from atomic record field support, by [Joe Kerrigan](https://github.com/joe-kerrigan) ([#6667](https://github.com/oxcaml/oxcaml/pull/6667))
- `Atomic.t` and `Atomic.Loc.t` operations (`set`, `exchange`, `compare_and_set`, `compare_exchange`) switched from `@ local` to `[@local_opt]` annotations, allowing the compiler to specialize these externals for both local and global references ([#6667](https://github.com/oxcaml/oxcaml/pull/6667))
- New `-gno-ocamldebug-types` command-line flag (via `Clflags.debug_ocamldebug_types`) lets users drop bytecode typing information from debug output by [Stephen Dolan](https://github.com/stedolan) ([#6706](https://github.com/oxcaml/oxcaml/pull/6706))
- Warning 211 was reworked from `Mod_by_top` into a structured `Redundant_modifier` variant carrying a `Default_bound`/`Implied_by` reason, improving redundant-modifier diagnostics by [@dkalinichenko-js](https://github.com/dkalinichenko-js) ([#5436](https://github.com/oxcaml/oxcaml/pull/5436))
- Coercions from `external`s to `[@@zero_alloc] val`s are now permitted, easing use of zero-alloc-checked externals across module boundaries, by [James Rayman](https://github.com/jra4) ([#6651](https://github.com/oxcaml/oxcaml/pull/6651))
- `or_null`-based custom variants can now carry void null payloads by [@julesjacobs](https://github.com/julesjacobs) ([#6383](https://github.com/oxcaml/oxcaml/pull/6383))
- csel/cmov code generation was optimized further by [@ttebbi-janestreet](https://github.com/ttebbi-janestreet) ([#6659](https://github.com/oxcaml/oxcaml/pull/6659))
- Fixed a GC pacing bug affecting programs with large off-heap data by [Stephen Dolan](https://github.com/stedolan) ([#6749](https://github.com/oxcaml/oxcaml/pull/6749))
- Fixed a bug involving the interaction of effects, callbacks, and local allocations by [Stephen Dolan](https://github.com/stedolan) ([#5747](https://github.com/oxcaml/oxcaml/pull/5747))
- Debug-info generation performance was improved by [Simon Spies](https://github.com/spiessimon) ([#5124](https://github.com/oxcaml/oxcaml/pull/5124)), and the x86 binary emitter now avoids eagerly resolving `.reloc` directives ([#6009](https://github.com/oxcaml/oxcaml/pull/6009))
- Generic apply/curry functions now use immutable loads for closure fields by [Mark Shinwell](https://github.com/mshinwell) ([#6508](https://github.com/oxcaml/oxcaml/pull/6508)), and `Dwarf_low`/`Dwarf_high` gained miscellaneous additions ([#6505](https://github.com/oxcaml/oxcaml/pull/6505))
- `HACKING.md` gained an "Updating Merlin" section documenting the vendored `external/merlin` frontend sync workflow and its CI check, alongside updates to `external/merlin/HACKING.jst.md` ([#6735](https://github.com/oxcaml/oxcaml/pull/6735), [#6760](https://github.com/oxcaml/oxcaml/pull/6760))
- The unboxed-types block-indices manual page was revised to match the current atomic-field behavior ([#6667](https://github.com/oxcaml/oxcaml/pull/6667))

repositories.trends_summary: Continued internal rework of flambda2 int-id/rec-info tracking, atomic primitive build-out, and the vendored Merlin sync workflow.
repositories.emerging_trends:
- **Flambda2 internal rework** around int-id tracking and rec-info correctness continued as a multi-PR effort by [Basile Clément](https://github.com/bclement-ocp), spanning lazy renaming during import, serialization of `Cached_level.t`, and join/simplification of rec-info aliases, and closed two long-running tracking issues ([#6695](https://github.com/oxcaml/oxcaml/issues/6695), [#4405](https://github.com/oxcaml/oxcaml/issues/4405), [#6715](https://github.com/oxcaml/oxcaml/pull/6715), [#6750](https://github.com/oxcaml/oxcaml/pull/6750), [#6754](https://github.com/oxcaml/oxcaml/pull/6754), [#6759](https://github.com/oxcaml/oxcaml/pull/6759), [#6770](https://github.com/oxcaml/oxcaml/pull/6770), [#6771](https://github.com/oxcaml/oxcaml/pull/6771), [#6772](https://github.com/oxcaml/oxcaml/pull/6772), [#6773](https://github.com/oxcaml/oxcaml/pull/6773), [#6774](https://github.com/oxcaml/oxcaml/pull/6774))
- **Atomic primitives** for records, block indices, and now pointers are being built out incrementally by [Joe Kerrigan](https://github.com/joe-kerrigan) over consecutive weeks, moving from record fields ([#6677](https://github.com/oxcaml/oxcaml/pull/6677)) to block indices ([#6667](https://github.com/oxcaml/oxcaml/pull/6667)) to full pointer support opened this week ([#6743](https://github.com/oxcaml/oxcaml/pull/6743), [#6746](https://github.com/oxcaml/oxcaml/pull/6746), [#6747](https://github.com/oxcaml/oxcaml/pull/6747))
- The vendored **Merlin sync** became a documented, first-class workflow this week (`HACKING.md`, `external/merlin/HACKING.jst.md`, CI moved into `build.yml`), reflecting ongoing effort to keep the editor-support frontend in step with compiler frontend changes ([#6735](https://github.com/oxcaml/oxcaml/pull/6735), [#6757](https://github.com/oxcaml/oxcaml/pull/6757), [#6760](https://github.com/oxcaml/oxcaml/pull/6760), [#6765](https://github.com/oxcaml/oxcaml/pull/6765), [#6778](https://github.com/oxcaml/oxcaml/pull/6778))
- **Reaper** cross-module dependency resolution via `.cmr`/`.ltosol` files progressed with plumbing and file I/O landing this week, ahead of the actual solving logic ([#6641](https://github.com/oxcaml/oxcaml/pull/6641), [#6725](https://github.com/oxcaml/oxcaml/pull/6725), [#6731](https://github.com/oxcaml/oxcaml/pull/6731), [#6752](https://github.com/oxcaml/oxcaml/pull/6752))
- Agent-assisted development practices are becoming visible in the workflow itself, with a persistent-watcher dev loop and its failure-path hardening explicitly informed by "five independent experience reports from sessions that each built one piece of a compiler project" ([#6786](https://github.com/oxcaml/oxcaml/pull/6786), [#6794](https://github.com/oxcaml/oxcaml/pull/6794))

group_summaries.brief_summary: MirageOS/Solo5 releases, a prometheus core/Lwt split, and OCaml Workshop 2026 site build-out defined ecosystem activity this week.
group_summaries.new_features_summary: New affect, dune-rpc-eio, and prometheus-lwt packages, mirage-xen grant-copy support, and a new OCaml Workshop 2026 schedule page.
group_summaries.new_features:
- New **affect** 0.0.0 package published, a streamlined effects-based concurrency model for OCaml supported by an OCaml Software Foundation grant, by [Daniel Bünzli](https://github.com/dbuenzli) ([ocaml/opam-repository#30469](https://github.com/ocaml/opam-repository/issues/30469))
- New **dune-rpc-eio** 0.1.0 package: an Eio client for dune's RPC protocol that can spawn or attach to a dune server, build paths/aliases, run tests, and read diagnostics, by [Anil Madhavapeddy](https://github.com/avsm) ([ocaml/opam-repository#30453](https://github.com/ocaml/opam-repository/issues/30453))
- **prometheus** 1.4 splits the library into a synchronous core and a new **prometheus-lwt** package, deprecating the Lwt-typed timing helpers in core ahead of their eventual removal, by [Anil Madhavapeddy](https://github.com/avsm) with [Mark Elvers](https://github.com/mtelvers) ([ocaml/opam-repository#30452](https://github.com/ocaml/opam-repository/issues/30452))
- **mirage-xen** 9.0.1 adds `Import.copy_from`/`Import.copy_to`, hypervisor-mediated grant-copy primitives that speed up transfers such as the qubes-mirage-firewall, by [Hannes Mehnert](https://github.com/hannesm) ([ocaml/opam-repository#30493](https://github.com/ocaml/opam-repository/issues/30493))
- **jsont** 0.3.0 narrows the safely encodable integer range for `Jsont.int`/`Jsont.int64` from `[-2^53;2^53]` to `[-2^53+1;2^53-1]` (a breaking change; legacy variants provided for migration), and fixes nested out-of-order case-member decoding, by [Daniel Bünzli](https://github.com/dbuenzli) ([ocaml/opam-repository#30485](https://github.com/ocaml/opam-repository/issues/30485))
- **sqlite3** 5.4.2 fixes OCaml GC rooting across runtime-released SQLite calls, preventing statement/database wrappers from being finalized while blocked inside SQLite, by [Markus Mottl](https://github.com/mmottl) ([ocaml/opam-repository#30475](https://github.com/ocaml/opam-repository/issues/30475))
- **ocamlmig** updated to OCaml 5.5 and its `[@@migrate]` attribute now accepts a `~min_version` for dependencies, by [v-gb](https://github.com/v-gb) ([ocaml/opam-repository#30396](https://github.com/ocaml/opam-repository/issues/30396))
- New packages published this week: **checked_oint** 2.1.0 checked integer arithmetic by [@hirrolot](https://github.com/hirrolot) ([ocaml/opam-repository#30505](https://github.com/ocaml/opam-repository/issues/30505)); **bitflyer** and **gmocoin** cryptocurrency-exchange API clients by [YOSHIHIRO Imai](https://github.com/yoshihiro503) ([ocaml/opam-repository#30459](https://github.com/ocaml/opam-repository/issues/30459), [ocaml/opam-repository#30460](https://github.com/ocaml/opam-repository/issues/30460)); the 4-package pure-OCaml Neo4j driver **neodriver** by [Tomasz Barański](https://github.com/tomob) ([ocaml/opam-repository#30448](https://github.com/ocaml/opam-repository/issues/30448)); and **p4spectec** 0.1.2, a P4-language mechanization toolchain, by [Haechan Kwon](https://github.com/pacokwon) ([ocaml/opam-repository#30455](https://github.com/ocaml/opam-repository/issues/30455))
- Added a dedicated **OCaml Workshop 2026 schedule page** at `/ocaml-workshop-2026/schedule`, wiring up a new `Schedule` section in the workshop navigation layout, URL, handler, and router, by [Sudha Parimala](https://github.com/Sudha247) ([ocaml/ocaml.org#3740](https://github.com/ocaml/ocaml.org/issues/3740)), followed by speaker authors, talk abstracts, and a timing fix ([ocaml/ocaml.org#3742](https://github.com/ocaml/ocaml.org/issues/3742))
